axes.model_access:
**The official docs list 5 model-access paths** (docs/src/ai/llm-providers.md):

- Zed-Hosted Models — billed through Zed
- API Access — your own provider quota, including Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI-compatible
- Existing Subscription — reuse a paid ChatGPT / Claude / Copilot etc.
- Gateway — routed via gateways like OpenRouter / Bedrock / Vercel
- **Local Model** — running locally or self-hosted

**Path choice is up to the user, not a bound single provider.** `llm-providers.md` lists these five item by item.
axes.runtime:
**A local desktop application, written in Rust.**

The official self-description: from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter, leading with performance and multiplayer collaboration.

**Verification record**: the docs include `dev-containers.md` (dev containers).
There is also a `toolchains.md` (toolchain management) page.

Closing the app stops it.
axes.local_files:
Reads and writes the workspace directly, **with multi-root support**.

Can also open remote folders via SSH / WSL, i.e. remote development.

File-tree scanning is controlled by `file_scan_exclusions` and `project_panel.hide_gitignore`.
Symbol capability comes from Tree-sitter parsing and language servers (LSP).
Edit prediction has its own separate provider.

The agent's built-in retrieval has four kinds: grep (regex), find_path (glob), list_directory, read_file.

**No codebase vectorized semantic index found officially** (Tools page checked).

**The official docs state the large-repo limit explicitly**:
huge directories with >100,000 files open at once perform poorly.
The official advice is to open only specific projects or subdirectories (remote development page).
axes.background:
A local desktop app; agent threads run inside the local process.
Remote hosts can be your own SSH / WSL hosts.

**Bound to the client being online.**
While a thread runs, Zed asks the system not to sleep.
This preserves long turns (`agent.prevent_idle_sleep`).

Remote development puts language servers, tasks and terminals on **your own remote server**.
The official docs note **since v0.157 it no longer relays through Zed servers**.

**No "keeps running after shutdown / vendor-hosted background task" capability found officially** (Agent Panel page checked).
axes.tools:
**MCP support is explicit.**

The official docs `mcp.md` states **Tools and Prompts** are the two supported protocol features.
Discovery / Sampling / Elicitation are not yet covered; the official docs welcome contributions.

It also handles `notifications/tools/list_changed` — when a server adds/removes/changes tools at runtime,
Zed reloads the list automatically without restarting the server.

MCP has two integration paths:

- install as an extension
- add local / remote servers under Settings → AI → MCP Servers

Popular extension servers listed officially: Context7, GitHub, Puppeteer, Gem,
Brave Search, Framelink Figma, Resend and more.
axes.context:
**Zed Agent's context is composed of instructions + skills + MCP** (see the Zed Agent row in agents.md).

**Compaction policy**: officially, threads auto-compact when approaching the threshold.
Default trigger at 90% (`agent.auto_compact`).
It summarizes earlier messages and replaces them in the model context.
The thread shows "Context Compacted", expandable.

`/compact` also compacts manually.
The threshold is configurable: percentage / positive tokens / negative remaining tokens.

When the model window is too small (<80000 tokens) auto-compaction is disabled.
The official hint is to start a new thread via New From Summary.

@-mention can add files, directories, symbols, past threads, skills, diagnostics, branch diffs and URLs.

Parallel multi-threads (each with its own context window) and Checkpoints per-message rollback are also supported.
axes.permissions:
**Tool permissions are controlled by Zed's official config** (`tool-permissions` page; since v0.224.0
by `agent.tool_permissions.default`).

Three values: `"allow"` / `"deny"` / `"confirm"`, with default set to confirm.
Per-tool regex patterns can be configured: `always_allow` / `always_deny` / `always_confirm`.

Precedence: always_deny > always_confirm > always_allow > tool default > global default.

There are also hardcoded safety rules (`rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~` etc.), **not overridable**.

Managed tools include:

- terminal, edit_file, write_file
- delete_path, move_path, copy_path, create_directory
- fetch, search_web, skill
- MCP (`mcp:<server>:<tool>`)

**There is also an OS-level sandbox** (`sandboxing` page): Zed Agent only, covering `terminal` and `fetch`,
restricting writes outside the project and outbound network by default.

**Permission boundaries follow the agent path** (agents.md):

- Zed Agent — uses Zed-configured providers and native tools
- External Agents — use the ACP agent process's own auth/config
- Terminal Threads — use the native CLI's auth/config

Privacy: officially Zed states it does not store prompts or code context; telemetry can be turned off.
axes.fit:
Fits scenarios that value editor performance (Rust), parsing accuracy (Tree-sitter) and multiplayer collaboration.

**Also fits users who want to mix multiple CLI Agents in one editor**
— Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Copilot / Cursor can all be attached.

This is Zed's most unique value: it is an **orchestration layer** for agents, not a single agent.

Does not fit users looking for "the editor ships its own AI" as the sole selling point — Zed positions itself as the orchestration layer.

Also does not fit people who need measured runs to know large-repo behavior — the indexing strategy is not disclosed officially.

sections.最重要的发现：Zed 自己就用「harness」这个词:
**The official `agents.md` treats "agent path" and "harness" as the same thing.**

**Official wording**: "An agent path is sometimes called **a harness**." "It is the way agentic work is started, displayed, configured, and controlled in Zed."

**This sentence lands AgentClash's "Harness chapter" into product documentation.**
Comparing Agent products and comparing Harnesses are not two different things.
AgentClash distinguishes them because they sit at different layers.
And Zed explicitly says **"an agent path is sometimes called a harness"**.
sections.三类 agent path（官方表格原文）:
| Agent path | Runs in | Uses | Fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Zed Agent** | Agent Panel + Threads sidebar | Zed-configured LLM providers, native tools, skills, instructions, MCP | wanting Zed's native integration |
| **External Agents** | Agent Panel + Threads sidebar | **the ACP agent process and its own auth/config** | wanting Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor, Pi etc. |
| **Terminal Threads** | Threads sidebar + terminal | **the native CLI / TUI's auth/config** | keeping that tool's command-line experience |

**This table carries a lot of information**:

- External Agents explicitly support **Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor** — all objects collected in this repository
- **who decides permissions — look at columns two and three** — choose External Agent and auth/config belongs to that agent
- Zed positions itself as the layer for "how agents are started, displayed, configured, controlled"
sections.五条模型接入路径（这个分区独一份）:
| Path | Fits | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| **Zed-Hosted Models** | letting Zed bill on your behalf | Account & Billing |
| **API Access** | already have provider quota | includes Anthropic-compatible / OpenAI-compatible |
| **Existing Subscription** | **already paying for ChatGPT / Claude / Copilot** | reuse the subscription |
| **Gateway** | routing via OpenRouter / Bedrock / Vercel | gateway config |
| **Local Model** | **running locally or self-hosted** | local config |

**Paths 3 and 5 are the differentiators**:

- reusing an existing subscription = marginal cost can be 0
- local models = data never leaves the machine

**Another distinction the official docs make explicit**:

**Official wording**: "Model access paths do not configure External Agents or Terminal Threads." "External Agents and Terminal Threads usually own their own model access, auth, and configuration."

**That is: Zed's model settings do not reach external agents.** This is an easy point to misunderstand.
sections.MCP 支持的确切范围:
| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| **Tools** | ✅ supported |
| **Prompts** | ✅ supported |
| Discovery / Sampling / Elicitation | ❌ not yet covered (contributions welcome officially) |
| `notifications/tools/list_changed` | ✅ handled — a server changing its tool list at runtime **auto-reloads, no restart** |

**Two integration paths**:

1. install as an **extension** (officially listed: Context7 / GitHub / Puppeteer / Gem / Brave Search / Figma / Resend etc.)
2. add local or remote servers under **Settings → AI → MCP Servers**

**MCP behaves differently across the three agent paths**:

| agent path | MCP behavior |
|---|---|
| Zed Agent | uses Zed-configured MCP servers directly |
| External Agents | Zed **can forward configured servers via ACP**; the agent can also read its own native MCP config |
| Terminal Threads | **the native CLI/TUI reads its own MCP config** |
sections.与本站其他站点的关系:
Zed's External Agents directly involve multiple objects collected in this repository:

| agent path in Zed | corresponding entries in this repository |
|---|---|
| External Agents list | [Claude Code](./claude-code.md) · [Codex IDE](./codex-ide.md) · [Cline](./cline.md) · [Copilot](./copilot.md) · [Cursor](./cursor.md) |
| Terminal Threads | CLI-form objects in this repository's [agents section](../_category.md) |
| MCP extensions | [tools section](../../mcp/_category.md) |

**This makes Zed a crossroads of this repository.**
It draws the boundary between the two forms of the agents section (IDE extension / terminal) and the tools section (MCP extensions) most clearly.
